simple.meaning: יָלַךְ (yâlak) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to walk (literally or figuratively); causatively, to carry (in various senses).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1044 times in Genesis, Exodus, beginning at Genesis 3:14. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, Torah, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָלַךְ (H3212) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָלַךְ (yâlak) / H3212 is traced through Genesis 3:14, Genesis 7:18, Genesis 9:23, Genesis 11:31 with source-language evidence and verse context.
